persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Gabbs, James I1.' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 5 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1). THE INITIAL IN THIS NAME CANNOT BE READ, AND THAT IS THE RULING (T-0721). The name carries a DIGIT, and a digit is never part of a name: it is what the OCR left where the compositor set an initial. No run here can go back to the column and read the letter, because the Chicago Democrat's page images are held OUTSIDE this repository — the source record says so and registers the deposit as text_only. So no letter is written here and none may be; T-0638's suspicions register reached the same conclusion and set `suspected_reading: null` on this token. The name stands exactly as the paper's transcription gives it. What has changed is that the illegible initial no longer refuses the whole reading: tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py drops the ruled token, for this name and no other, so the legible part can be clustered, and the unread initial is absent from every key, so no identity is merged on it. The ruling, the impressions it rests on and the reason a letter is refused are in data/research/residents/letter_list_unread_initials.json, and tools/check_unread_initial_rulings.py fails the build if this card's name moves out from under it or if a row ever acquires a letter. The `I1.` stands for the middle initial. Only one impression is in hand; the surviving transcription of the 8 July issue is partial and does not carry this stretch of the list. `I1` is the shape an `H` leaves when its crossbar drops out, and equally the shape of a broken `N`, `M` or `U`, and this project will not choose among them. The card now stands on `James Gabbs` as identity id_gabbs_james, alone.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
